frames.review_note: Clean. Standing ranks of bare-chested nobles in mundus and shoulder cloths, brass open-wick lamps doubled in the polished floor, carved pillars, open outer doorway with a silver sheet of rain, sanctum shown only as gold fragments. No painted text. Captions fit in the dark ceiling and pillar-capital band across the top and on the low-detail floor at lower right.

Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch28 temple row: Kerala topknot with grey at the temples, no turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold stud, silver chain with a medallion, a cream mundu and shoulder cloth on a bare chest, no forehead marks and no sacred thread. Two nobles in front of him glance at him sidelong, so the beat works. Weaker points: this assembly is SEATED, while 1.1 and the chosen 1.2 show standing ranks. Nagoji also faces the camera while the men behind him face away toward the sanctum. That reads as a portrait staging, not as him standing behind the rank. The young noble at right wears loose long curly hair, not a topknot. He has no moustache, so he does not read as a Nagoji double. Captions go in the upper corners over the pillar carvings at top-left and the sanctum and lamps at top-right, clear of all three faces. No text, no blood and hands are sound. Acceptable given it is the only candidate. Regenerate later only if the author wants the hall standing throughout.

Acceptable. Varma matches the aged dedication sheet: grey hair drawn back into a low knot, moustache, bare torso with the sacred thread, plain white mundu, no jewels or headwear. He enters from the rain-filled far doorway, the silk-wrapped hilt and flame-lit blade held across his body, and every noble's head is turned toward him. Minor issues: he grips the hilt in his right hand with the blade resting on his left palm, rather than lying flat across both palms; the mundu has a thin gold hem border; the nobles are seated, while 1.1 has them standing. No painted text. The two captions fit in the dark carved pillar areas at the top, to the left and right of the doorway, clear of faces.

Clean. Varma seen from behind (grey low knot, bare back, sacred thread, white mundu with a thin gold hem border, no jewels) walks alone up the lamp-lined aisle between seated ranks of nobles, sword held level across his hands; chief priest at the far end matches the V13 temple-priest face, the other chanting priests are bearded and distinct. Rain only through the open outer doorway, as the setting specifies. Two grey-haired nobles in the ranks are older men, not Varma doubles. The dark ceiling between the pillars (top centre, roughly x 0.38 to 0.75, y 0.0 to 0.22) takes both captions clear of faces.

Clean. Varma from behind at the sanctum threshold (grey low knot, bare back, sacred thread, plain white mundu with a thin gold hem, no jewels), sword held level; through the gold doors only fragments of Padmanabha (a resting hand and forearm on the serpent coils) under five rising hoods, drawn reverently, never the whole god. He is less dwarfed than the script suggests, but the tall doors carry the scale. Same mandapa, lamps and rain-filled outer doorway as panel 1. Dark ceiling at upper left (x 0.05 to 0.3, y 0.0 to 0.2) holds the caption.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Acceptable with minor notes. Varma matches the aged dedication look (grey hair gathered in a knot at the back, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, sacred thread, bare torso, white mundu, no jewels), kneeling with head bowed, the sword across both open palms pointing toward the sanctum, which leads cleanly into 2.5; hands are sound. A foreground brass lamp with a bending flame sits at lower right as scripted. Minor: the nobles behind him are sharp, not out of focus, and they stand, while panel 1 showed seated ranks; the lead noble (dark-grey hair, curled moustache, gold necklaces and armbands) slightly echoes Varma's younger court look but is clearly a different man. Dark ceiling at top centre (x 0.3 to 0.65, y 0.0 to 0.15) holds the caption.

The framing is a medium shot of the whole kneeling figure, wider than the scripted tight strip on the hands. His moustache reads thinner and greyer than in 2.4. Accepted because the beat is clear: his hands lower a bare steel blade, point toward the sanctum, with a red silk-wrapped hilt that matches 1.5. The grey low knot, sacred thread, plain mundu and setting all match. Captions can sit over the shadowed pillars along the top or on the floor at lower left without touching his face, his hands or the sword.

Minor: a tiny gold speck just under the nose tip, at the top of the moustache (about 5 px at full size). It reads as a highlight at print size, but paint it out if it shows as a nose ornament. The mundu has gold kasavu borders rather than plain white, which matches the page 2 frames. Otherwise this is the aged varma-v1 face: grey hair in a low knot at the nape, sacred thread, bare torso, kneeling and lit gold from the sanctum, with rain in the outer doorway. There is no painted text, and the dark ceiling at top left and centre gives room for both balloons.

Clean. The wide shot is taken over the seated nobles' heads. Varma kneels small and bright at the far end, seen from behind, with a grey low knot, the sacred thread and a white mundu. The dark ceiling band above the sanctum and the upper pillars leaves room for the two balloons to run back toward the viewer.

Clean. Only the central chief priest carries the temple-priest sheet face; the other chanting priests have moustaches or beards and read as different men. In the foreground, the old noble has wet eyes and parted lips, with his hands joined in prayer, and the hands are sound. Both captions fit at the top corners, over the rain doorway on the left and the lamp tops on the right, clear of the raised hands.

Minor: Nagoji's jaw has light stubble shading, but there is no beard, and the curled moustache, small flush gold stud, topknot and grey temple are all correct. The silver chain of office shows clearly across his back. The chief's tuft sits at the crown rather than the front. The chief is heavy-set and shaven, with heavy gold ear-rings, a red-bordered shoulder cloth and grey stubble, and he leans right with a cupped hand toward the young, loose-haired neighbour. The balloon can sit in the upper band of pillars between Nagoji and the chief.

Minor: the clear space for the two balloons is the upper band above the heads (y below about 0.18), which is dark pillar and rain-doorway background and slightly tight; the chief's front tuft sits toward the crown rather than strictly at the front. Nagoji appears only as a shoulder and chest with the silver chain and medallion at the left edge, as the script asks. The chief matches panel 3.4: hoop earrings, red-bordered cloth, grey stubble, hand cupped at his mouth. Same mandapa, lamps and rain-lit outer doorway as 3.4. No painted text, balloons or anachronisms.

Clean. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, receding hair, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus, hands sound. He stands among the bowed rows with the sanctum behind him at right, and his eyes are on the rows. A noble at right lifts his chin, which fits the script's 'a lifted chin there'. The open outer doorway shows rain, as the setting requires. The caption fits the dark pillar and ceiling area in the upper middle. Minor: the nobles here are bowed low on the floor, while in 4.3 they sit and in 4.5 they stand.

Acceptable. Nagoji shows the Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a small flush gold ear stud, a silver chain, a bare chest with shoulder cloth and no forehead marks. His chin reads clean-shaven: there is only the faint ink hatching of the house style, no beard. He looks aside toward the sanctum side. Minor: the lamplight is more even across his face than the 'half his face' the script asks for, and the shoulder cloth has a gold stripe. Both captions fit in the dark carved ceiling area at the upper right (about x 0.6 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.22) without touching his face.

Acceptable, with minor issues. Varma, aged varma-v1, is rising from one knee with a hand on his knee: grey low knot, moustache, sacred thread, no jewels. The young attendant has a small knot and steps in holding a bundle of thin ribs. Nobles on both sides whisper behind raised hands. Minor: (1) Varma's and the attendant's mundus have a thin gold border rather than plain white, though the neighbouring ch28 frames draw Varma the same way. (2) The sword on the stone is drawn as an ornate gold sheathed sword, not the bare blade with a red silk hilt from 2.5, and it lies behind him to the left rather than clearly at the sanctum threshold. (3) The broom ribs are pale straw here and darker brown in 4.4 and 4.5. The caption fits the upper middle among the dark pillar tops.

v03 (the newest version) is acceptable. It is a tight handover of a handleless coconut-rib broom bound with coir, with ragged tips, passing from the attendant to Varma in the same lamplit mandapa as 4.3 and 4.5: granite pillars, brass open-wick lamps, rain through the outer doorway on the right. Varma is cropped just below the mouth. Only his chin, neck and a grey low knot at the back show, with bare torso, sacred thread and plain white mundu, and no jewels. All four hands are sound. There is no text, no blood and nothing anachronistic. The panel has no lettering. Minor faults: (1) The inking is flatter and cleaner than the more painterly 4.3 and 4.5. (2) The visible chin has light grey stubble, which hardly shows at inset size. (3) The attendant's mundu is plain white, while in 4.3 it has a thin gold edge. The other versions are worse. v01 shows Varma's whole face with no moustache, which breaks his sheet, and it is wider than the script's 'inset, tight'. v02 is photorealistic, which breaks the style rule.

Acceptable. Aged Varma kneels low before the golden sanctum doors, sweeping scattered flower petals with a short handleless rib broom: moustache, grey low knot, sacred thread, white mundu, hands sound. In the background the nobles stand frozen with their hands dropped and clasped and their mouths closed. Rain shows through the outer doorway. The frame is the required 3:1 strip, and the faces sit in the middle band. Minor: he is down on both knees rather than one, and his mundu has the thin gold border used throughout the chapter. The caption fits the dark ceiling and pillar tops in the upper middle (about x 0.42 to 0.6, y 0.02 to 0.18).

Minor only: Varma is in the middle distance, not the very small far figure the script asks for, and the high angle is moderate. Grey low knot, sacred thread, moustache, no jewels, short coconut-rib broom held mid-stroke, nobles at the edges, rain on the grove past the outer wall. The upper frame is busy with pillars, so both captions belong on the clear lamplit floor in the lower centre (x 0.25-0.80, y 0.65-0.95), which has no faces.

Minor: the chief has a short grey beard rather than stubble, and his look is a troubled hand-to-chin frown, which still reads as the knowing look gone. Varma kneels with the short broom, has a grey low knot and sacred thread, and wears no jewels. The sanctum shows only gold fragments, with no whole idol. The caption can sit in the dark low-detail area at top centre (x 0.48-0.73, y 0.0-0.13).

Minor: the broom here is a longer bundle than the short broom in panels 1-2, though it is still handleless coconut ribs. A soft gold idol-like shape shows through the sanctum door, but it is blurred, partial and half hidden by the attendant, so it reads as fragments of gold. Varma's mundu is dusty and his hands are ash-grey. He has a grey low knot at the nape and the sacred thread. The attendant is young and slight, with a short mundu and a small top knot. No lettering is needed.

None significant. Varma has turned to the assembly and looks toward the viewer from Nagoji's point of view. He has a grey low knot, the sacred thread and a dust-marked mundu, and wears no jewels. Nagoji is not drawn. The long caption fits in the dark empty ceiling at top right (x 0.55-0.88, y 0.0-0.18).

Minor: several chanting priests stand upright beside Varma, which softens 'the one head not bowed', though he is still the central, framed figure. The sword lies beside rather than directly behind his feet. The bowing chief shows his shaven head and red-bordered cloth but no visible gold ear-rings. Only the lamp-bearing chief priest has the temple-priest face, so there are no doubles. Lettering space is tight. Put the PRIESTS balloon over the rain at top left (x 0.04-0.14, y 0.0-0.15), with its tail to the lamp-bearing chief priest. Put the captions over the anonymous bowed backs in the bottom-left and bottom-right corners (y 0.85-1.0), clear of the chief, Varma and the sword.

Clean. Revathi matches her sheet and bible row (indigo and gold sari, grey streak, jasmine braid, coin necklace, tali on yellow thread, armlets, sandalwood line). Nagoji in the doorway matches (white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain, sword, grey topknot, curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud). Banner is plain red with a silver conch and no lettering. Open sky at upper centre takes both captions.

Minor: up close there is faint mottled shading on the jaw, but it reads as clean-shaven at panel size. The banner hangs straight down from a crossbar instead of flying as in the other panels. Otherwise good: set jaw, diagonal shadow across the coat, grey topknot, tiny flush gold stud, uniform and chain. Sky between his head and the banner leaves room for the two off-panel balloons; tails point to the right edge, where he is looking.

Minor: the tali hangs on a thin gold cord instead of a clearly yellow thread. Her expression reads a little troubled more than purely weary. The head turn is a sideways glance rather than a full turn, but the beat still reads. Otherwise clean: she matches her sheet (indigo and gold sari, jasmine braid, grey threading, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line). The courtyard, gatehouse and conch banner match the page, with no text on the banner, and the brass lamps have open wicks. Nagoji is correctly off-panel; he is placed off the left edge, toward the doorway and her gaze. The sky band across the top centre and right has room for all three short balloons.

Clean. Close on Revathi with a startled, newly seeing look toward Nagoji at frame right. All her bible details are present, including visible grey threading. Nagoji in the background matches (white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain, grey topknot, curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud). He is drawn sharp, not soft, which is acceptable. Nagoji is visible, so the tail for his 'off' line goes to his mouth. Sky across the top leaves room for three balloons.

Clean. Wide two-shot across a long stretch of flagstone in the fort courtyard. The tiled gatehouse and the red conch banner are in place, in low gold evening light. Nagoji is in the white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain and boots, with a grey-streaked topknot, no turban, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small gold stud. Revathi is in the indigo-and-gold sari with the jasmine braid, grey threading, tali pendant, gold armlets and sandalwood line. Brass oil lamps have open flames. There is open sky in the upper centre for both balloons.

Acceptable. Revathi turns a step toward the open gate with her face in profile against the sunset. The courtyard, gatehouse, conch banner and lighting match panel 1. One small oddity: her tali-style pendant hangs down her back, not her front. It does not read as an error at panel size. The sky upper right, between her head and the flag, holds both balloons.

Acceptable. Revathi turns back over her shoulder toward the viewer and Nagoji, who is off-panel. The courtyard and gatehouse match the page. Her grey threading, jasmine braid, armlets, bangles and sandalwood line are correct, and her hand is sound. Again the pendant thread falls at her back (minor). There is sky upper right for her two balloons. Nagoji's balloon tails off the right edge, where he stood in panel 1.

Clean. Tight on Revathi with the flat-coin necklace, tali on its yellow thread, jhumkas, jasmine braid, grey threading, sandalwood line and gold armlets. The same gatehouse and banner sit at sunset behind her. The panel on the gatepost is a blank carved relief, not text. There is sky in the upper centre and upper right for both balloons.

Clean. Full-width final beat: Revathi walks out through the open gate into the low gold evening, small, with her back turned. Nagoji stands still in the near foreground, in the white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain and sword, with a grey-streaked topknot, no turban, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small gold stud. The conch banner flies above the gate. Upper-centre sky takes her two balloons trailing back toward him, and the open flagstones low in the centre take his caption.

Clean. Ramayyan matches his sheet: receding curly hair, thin features, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus at his elbow. The commissioner wears a bag-wig, lace stock and dark cuffed coat, signs with a quill, and his tricorn is on the table. The soldiers wear blue coats, the treaty sheet is blank and there is no lettering. Caption space is fairly tight: use the roof and sky band along the top, between the soldiers' heads, plus the plain tablecloth at the front if needed.

Acceptable. Nagoji: white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain, topknot with grey at the temples, curled moustache, clean chin and a small gold bead stud. Varma: aged face, grey low knot, shoulder cloth and sacred thread. Minor: Varma's mundu has a thin gold border instead of plain white, which is consistent with 8.3 and 8.4. There is a large clear night sky for the caption.

Acceptable. Varma is seen from behind at the wet parapet, looking out at the dark. He has a grey low knot and moustache, and the sacred thread shows across his back. The setting matches 8.2. Minor continuity point: the shoulder cloth from 8.2 is gone and he is bare-torsoed here, which fits the bible row and 8.4 and 8.5. There is wide sky above for both balloons.

Acceptable. Varma has turned from the parapet, his head turned toward the off-panel Nagoji. He has the aged face, grey low knot, sacred thread, no jewels and the same mundu as 8.2 and 8.3. Minor: the script's plain shoulder cloth is absent, consistent with 8.3 and 8.5. He has a white and red namam on his forehead, which matches his face-study sheet and is not banned for Varma. His hands are behind his back. The upper-right sky is clear for the balloon.

Minor: Varma's low knot is dark with grey streaks rather than fully grey as in 9.1 and 9.4. Otherwise on beat: close night face with a tear, sacred thread, plain shoulder cloth, wet parapet and camp lights. The memory bleeds in at the upper left as a ragged warm stain, not a framed flashback: young laughing Savitri, head thrown back, in a cream cloth with a red-and-gold border, gold earrings and necklace, no indigo, jasmine, tali or coin necklace. No painted text. Clear night sky upper right for the balloon.

Minor only. Varma matches the varma-v1 dedication face: grey low knot at the back, sacred thread, bare torso, no jewels or headwear. His head is in profile against the sky. One fist stays on the parapet while the other hand lies open, palm up, on the wet stone. Nagoji is small behind him and matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, topknot with grey at the temple, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain. However, he is drawn sharp rather than out of focus. Varma's mundu has gold border stripes where the bible says plain. Both are small deviations. The upper sky above and right of Varma's head is wide, open space for the long and short balloons.

Minor: at this small scale Nagoji's ear ornament reads as a tiny pale bead just under the lobe, not a flush gold stud. It is a few pixels wide, so retouch it to a flush gold stud if possible. Nagoji has no grey at the temples. Varma's mundu has a gold border rather than plain, which matches the rest of the page. Otherwise on beat: wide 3:1 strip, Varma's arm opening toward the dark kingdom, fort lamps on far hills, the pale road, the camp cookfires, two small figures on the wet wall walk, Nagoji with a clean-shaven chin and thick moustache in the white coat and red waistcoat. No painted text. Wide clear sky band across the top for the balloon and two captions.

Minor: the camera is inside the chapel looking out at Nagoji in the doorway, not outside looking in, so the cross hangs on the inside wall rather than above the outer door. The beat still reads: De Lannoy kneels at the front pew, Duarte stands at the altar with hands raised (no Roman collar tab, ink-stained fingers) and Nagoji waits outside by the doorpost. Nagoji is on model, with a curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, grey temples, topknot, red waistcoat and chain of office. The small brass altar crucifix and chalice are acceptable. The granite wall in the upper middle, between the door and Duarte, gives clear space for both captions.

Minor: De Lannoy's hair reads as pale ash-blond with only a little grey. He wears white breeches here but a mundu-like lower garment in 10.4. Otherwise clean: he has stepped out of the chapel and faces Nagoji, who stands at the doorpost with a curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, grey temple streak, topknot, chain of office and no turban. Sky in the upper left takes De Lannoy's balloon. The granite above the door, upper right, takes Nagoji's.

Minor only: De Lannoy's hair reads a touch more golden-blond than 'pale grey', and Duarte's hair is silver-grey rather than fully white. Both match the neighbouring panels on page 10 (10.1, 10.2, 10.4, 10.5), so the page stays consistent. Everything else is correct. Duarte stands in the chapel doorway behind De Lannoy, who is turned toward him in lost profile. Duarte shows the stoop, a plain black standing collar with no white tab, the small gold cross on a chain and ink-stained fingers on clasped, well-drawn hands. De Lannoy is clean-shaven, in a white coat over a buff waistcoat with no red. The setting matches the other page-10 panels: the same granite chapel with a wooden cross above the door, evening light, an altar and pews inside. There is no painted text. Lettering space: the caption fits in the sky and fort area at top left, and Duarte's balloon on the plain granite above the doorway (on either side of the wooden cross), clear of both faces and Duarte's hands.

Minor: De Lannoy wears a mundu-like white lower garment, as on his sheet, where 10.2 shows breeches. His hair reads as pale ash-blond with grey. Otherwise the beat is exact: his palm lies flat on the granite doorframe (a well-formed hand), his mouth is open in speech, and the fort walls rise behind him in evening light. The large sky in the upper left holds both balloons easily.

Minor: Duarte's ink-stained right hand is held low, about waist height, rather than lifted chest-high, and the sleeve is only slightly drawn back. It still reads clearly as a hand stopped between the two men, with Nagoji looking down at it. Both men match their sheets: Nagoji has the thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, the gold stud, a topknot with grey at the temples, the white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain. Duarte has white-grey hair, a plain standing collar with no tab, and the small cross. The setting is outside the chapel at evening, as on page 10. There is no painted text and the panel needs no lettering space.

Mostly clean. Duarte matches his sheet: gaunt lined face, swept grey hair with side curls, plain black cassock with a plain standing collar and no white tab, small gold cross on a thin chain. His raised right hand makes a sound two-finger blessing toward screen left (where Nagoji stands off panel) and shows ink stains; the lowered left hand is sound too. No text, noose or gore. Minor points: (1) his hair is steel grey rather than fully white. That matches the sheet but is a shade darker than the 'white-haired' present-scene note. (2) His eyes are cast down and tired rather than looking straight at Nagoji. That still reads as the quiet blessing. Lettering space: the open evening sky at upper left (about x 0 to 0.29, y 0 to 0.22) above the raised hand, plus the plain granite wall above his head (about x 0.29 to 0.46, y 0 to 0.17), can hold both balloons. Keep the lower balloon clear of the fingertips at about y 0.21. The exterior setting (chapel door, fort walls, evening sky) matches 11.4 and 11.5. v02 is almost identical, with slightly heavier ink spots on the hand.

De Lannoy's hair is ash-blond with grey streaks rather than a fully pale grey, but this falls within the range of the page 10 panels. Otherwise clean: both men half-smiling; De Lannoy clean-shaven in a worn white coat over a buff waistcoat; Duarte white-haired, his black standing collar closed with no white tab, small cross, ink-stained fingers. The chapel interior matches 11.1. The rafters and the plaster wall above the cross leave room for both balloons.

Minor: De Lannoy's hair reads ash-blond rather than pale grey, darker than in 11.3. His expression is a little stern for 'Quiet'. Otherwise the beat is right: tall, clean-shaven, in a worn and smudged white coat, looking back through the open chapel door at the floor before the altar. There is no text. The plain plaster wall above the cross and the stone arch in the upper area give room for the long balloon.

Minor: De Lannoy's hair is pale ash-blond, not clearly grey, but it matches his sheet and the page 10 frames. The order is right: De Lannoy, Nagoji, Duarte. De Lannoy's right hand grips Nagoji's forearm, and the grip hand is sound. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch28 uniform row: moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold stud, topknot, grey at the temple, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain. Duarte stands at right with ink-stained clasped hands, a small cross and no collar tab. The fort wall and evening sky are behind, with the chapel at left. There is no painted text. The lettering space is adequate but split across the sky: the long De Lannoy balloon fits in the sky between De Lannoy's head and Nagoji's topknot (top centre-left), the short one in the sky above and between Nagoji and Duarte, and the long caption in the large clear sky at top right beside Duarte's head.

Minor: the young officer's hair is a full curly bun at the crown rather than a small Nair tuft, but he reads clearly as a separate, younger, clean-shaven man with no moustache and no ear stud, in a white coat and red waistcoat. Nagoji matches the later-life sheet and bible row: grey-streaked topknot, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold stud, white gold-bordered mundu with the end over the shoulder, no coat or turban, leaning on the parapet. The scene is a dusk rampart with monsoon clouds and distant rain over the sea. Hands are sound, there is no painted text (the flag is plain white), no anachronism, and the upper sky gives open space for the caption and the officer's balloon.

Minor: the edges are sharp, not a soft faded memory bleed, so the bleed would have to come from the compositor. Two brass lamps sit at the table corners, off the map. The blue coastal marks read a little like small lakes. There is no lettering or pseudo-writing anywhere, and the colour regions (red, black, brown, blue marks, pale patches on the south-west coast, sea to the left) match the script.

Minor: the masthead flags are plain red with no visible conch at this scale (there is no lettering on them). The musketeers' white coats read as long white tunics. Everything else matches: a volley drill with cross-belts, the red silver-conch standard, the shore battery, horsemen in the surf and lateen-sail coastal craft. The dark cloud band across the top is clear for both captions.

Minor: the officer looks somewhat older and heavier than twenty, and his hair is a back knot rather than a small crown tuft. He is still round-faced, has no moustache and wears the white coat. This is a reverse angle, so the sea sits on the left, consistent with the parapet side. Nagoji's ear stud is flush and his chin is essentially clean.

Duarte is drawn grey-haired as on his sheet rather than the script's 'dark-haired' younger Duarte; the bible base line (grey hair in his fifties, which is how he looks in Ch1) overrides the script, so this is acceptable. Nagoji's ear stud reads as a tiny gold bead rather than a perfectly flush stud (minor at print size). The memory treatment is a faded torn-paper edge with fairly warm colour rather than strong desaturation. Otherwise clean: captivity costume, loose black hair with no grey, curled moustache, clean chin, wrists bound by rope to the stool, ankle irons, barefoot; rope is a coiled hank on an iron ring, no noose; no Roman collar tab; no painted text. Open stone wall in the upper centre between the two heads holds the balloon and two captions.

Minor: no sandalwood line visible at Revathi's hairline; Nagoji's expression is a faint closed-mouth smile. Otherwise matches: Revathi in indigo and gold with a jasmine braid, grey threading, the tali on a yellow thread, flat-coin necklace and gold armlets, turning with a raised finger toward the running niece; Nagoji behind her with a topknot, grey at the temples, a cream mundu and shoulder cloth, a silver chain, no knife, curled moustache, clean chin and ear stud. Brass open-wick lamps, wet stone, rain at the eaves, soft faded memory edges. Caption space: the dark rainy sky and eaves at upper right and the wall above the heads at top centre.

Minor: Revathi's braid is still mostly black below a grey crown, and her face reads only moderately aged. Otherwise correct: the split is down the middle under one rain, Kochi on the left and Velinadu on the right. Elderly Savitri is in plain white among banana plants and herb beds, with only a thin chain and no indigo, jasmine or tali. Revathi is on the verandah in indigo and gold with jasmine, the bead/coin necklace, armlets and a sandalwood mark. Laughing children run through the wet corridor, and there are no children in the Kochi half. The top bands of both halves (sky and eaves) hold the place tags; the roof and sky at upper right hold the extra caption.

Minor: a faint shadow of stubble on the chin (reads clean-shaven at print size), loose curls fall behind the grey-streaked topknot, and braziers burn in the rain. Otherwise matches the beat: Nagoji alone on the star-fort rampart, face lifted to the rain with eyes closed, a gold-bordered white mundu over one shoulder, no coat or turban, curled moustache and a flush gold ear stud. Below him are forts, roads, fields, the shore battery and a grey surf. The flags are plain cloth, there is no painted text, and both hands are sound. The broad stormy sky across the top holds all five captions.
